title: Tractatus
author: Ludwig Wittgenstein
scope: Seven main propositions (1–7), not the subsidiary propositions or complete book.
normalization: English PropositionE entries 1–7. Footnote about numbering omitted; whitespace reflowed; proposition 6 overbars rendered in Unicode. No paraphrasing.

passages.text: The world is everything that is the case.
passages.label: The world is everything that is the case.

passages.text: What is the case, the fact, is the existence of atomic facts.
passages.label: What is the case, the fact, is the existence of atomic facts.

passages.text: The logical picture of the facts is the thought.
passages.label: The logical picture of the facts is the thought.

passages.text: The thought is the significant proposition.
passages.label: The thought is the significant proposition.

passages.text: Propositions are truth-functions of elementary propositions. (An elementary proposition is a truth-function of itself.)
passages.label: Propositions are truth-functions of elementary propositions. (An elementary proposition is a truth-function of itself.)

passages.text: The general form of truth-function is: [p̄, ξ̄, N(ξ̄)]. This is the general form of proposition.
passages.label: The general form of truth-function is: [p̄, ξ̄, N(ξ̄)]. This is the general form of proposition.

passages.text: Whereof one cannot speak, thereof one must be silent.
passages.label: Whereof one cannot speak, thereof one must be silent.
